title: Domestication of the pig
summary: Pigs were first domesticated in southeastern Anatolia by 10,500–10,000 years ago, one of four major Near Eastern livestock species with sheep, goats and cattle. Clear changes in pig tooth size appear by about 9,500–9,000 years ago, and domestic pigs reached the southern Levant and lowland Iran by about 8,500–8,000 years ago. Early farmers carried them with other livestock across the Mediterranean, even by boat to Cyprus, and several domestic pig lineages trace back to the Near East.

uncertainty.note: Initial domestication 10,500–10,000 BP (Zeder 2008); domestic pigs in the southern Levant and lowland Iran by 8,500–8,000 BP.

as_recorded.value: pigs were first domesticated somewhere in southeastern Anatolia by 10,500–10,000 B.P.

where.modern_name: Southeastern Anatolia; reference pin at Çayönü, Turkey
where.historical_name: Upper Tigris and Euphrates basin in southeastern Anatolia during the Pre-Pottery Neolithic; no recorded polities or place names exist at this date

importance.justification: One of the four founding Near Eastern livestock species, still a major food animal (R3 D3 T4 L2).
